summary: Clarify matrix roles, decision rights and resource priorities through practical exercises. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Managing in a matrixed organization helps functional managers, project leads and team coordinators coordinate shared work across reporting lines. You will map dual accountabilities, clarify responsibilities with RACI and decision rights with RAPID, and plan resource negotiations and escalation paths. Exercises also cover stakeholder influence, conflict responses and feedback across matrix assignments, producing practical governance artefacts such as decision logs and a team charter.
audienceIntro: This foundation-level course suits professionals who coordinate work across functional and project reporting lines or need to make shared accountability clearer. It is designed for people who handle matrix decisions as part of their day-to-day responsibilities.
modules: Matrix Operating Models and Dual Reporting
Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Modes in Matrix Teams
prerequisites: No prior matrix-management training or coding is required. Familiarity with team, project or functional responsibilities will help you apply the exercises to your work.
